question.problem: If $[a]_{n}$ denotes the residue class containing all integers congruent to $a$ modulo $n,$ then $[-13]_{5}=$
question.worked_solution:
We have $[a]_{5}=[b]_{5}$ if 

$$
a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,5).
$$

The residue class $[-13]_{5}$ consists of the elements that are congruent to $-13$ modulo $5.$ 

We can find an alternative representation for this residue class as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[-13]_{5} & ={x\in Z\,|\,x≡-13\,(\text{mod}\,5)} \\  & ={x\in Z\,|\,x≡(-3)\cdot 5+2\,(\text{mod}\,5)} \\  & ={x\in Z\,|\,x≡(-3)\cdot 0+2\,(\text{mod}\,5)} \\  & ={x\in Z\,|\,x≡2\,(\text{mod}\,5)} \\  & =[2]_{5}\end{aligned}
$$
